pk.context: 25 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Only about 15% of an oral tablet reaches the circulation, mostly lost to first-pass metabolism.

clues.text: Bioavailability is about 15%, mostly lost to presystemic metabolism. Protein binding is low, about 14% to 21%, and a high-fat meal raises Cmax and AUC by 15% and 12%.
Supplied as the succinate salt; the active moiety has a molecular weight of 295.4 and is readily soluble in water and saline.
Approved under an NDA in 25, 50 and 100 mg tablets.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in ischemic coronary artery disease, prior stroke or TIA, and uncontrolled hypertension; atypical sensations and paresthesia are reported.
Acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults.
A selective agonist at 5-HT1B/1D receptors on intracranial blood vessels and trigeminal nerves, causing vessel constriction and inhibiting pro-inflammatory neuropeptide release.
The generic name begins with S and has eleven letters.
